acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Vampires family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Ancient, T4, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Signet-and-Membrane Salon Lord (Champion) archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two earth construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: An unnervingly still lord with an ageless corpse-white face, ornate rings on every long finger, a high formal collar, and a wide bat-membrane cloak divided into three ribbed panels.

Signature mechanic: Century Salon: the Ancient extends one ringed finger to tension a matching cloak rib. The Fang panel releases Thralls down a scent lane, the Hem panel curves a Bloodkin circle, and the Crest panel bends a Noble courtesy lane around the cloak. The active signet cannot close until the command resolves, leaving its finger and membrane joint exposed.
battlefieldDuty: Control several duel spaces by opening sections of a bat-membrane cloak with ringed fingers, screening hunters and redirecting blood-glass lanes through deliberate salon geometry.
constructionDimensions: The T1 Thrall retains its ragged silhouette with broken coffin splints at the shift knot and mineral-capped claws; T2–T5 regalia gains crypt-mineral structure through onyx signets, marble-white coffin plates, garnet blood-glass, slate coat weights, and faceted membrane braces scaled from coat hems to cloaks and wings.

Stance and movement become load-bearing through planted heel points, pendular cloak weights, fracture lines in the active crest or throne channel, and dust localized to hard stops rather than a constant wake.
counterplay: Read the bright signet, avoid the familiar rule within its panel, and strike either the extended finger or taut membrane joint; a torn panel removes that command and opens the salon sightline. Affinity signal: The onyx signet, cloak weight, or throne channel carrying a command develops a pale fracture after commitment; breaking it collapses that route and unbalances the otherwise perfect posture.
forbiddenTreatments: Palette-only earth treatment without crypt minerals, weighted silhouette, and changed load behavior
Glow-only earth treatment without a fracture, joint, or structural crest
Rock growth that buries corpse-white anatomy, tailored clothing, or bat membrane
Generic stone aristocrats with no feeding vessel, fangs, claws, or predatory recovery
identityInvariants: A tall or lengthening human silhouette retains corpse-white skin, long fingers, fangs, claws, red eyes, and an absence of warm living complexion.
Posture escalates from feral hunch to impossible stillness; higher forms widen through fitted coats, tailored cloaks, bat membrane, or shadow wings without obscuring humanlike anatomy.
Black, bone pallor, deep blood red, and aged gold remain paired with velvet, silk, brocade, polished leather, blood-glass, and bat membrane.
Blood is family-native feeding matter and lineage symbolism rather than Fire or Water affinity by itself; every use has a source, route, vessel, or recoverable feeding window.
Signet rings, high collars, jeweled clasps, medals, canes, blades, and family crests communicate authored encounter rank while exposing the hand, vessel, or crest that carries each command.
telegraph: The perfectly still face turns by a fraction, one ornate signet catches the available light, and the matching bat-membrane panel stretches between arm and cloak like a dark room divider.
